questions.title: Find the Set Root
questions.description:
A union-find forest stores every node's parent in an array (roots point to themselves: parent[x] == x). Return the root of x — follow parent pointers until you reach a self-parent. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n values parent[i] (0-based, roots satisfy parent[i] == i); line 3 has x. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int find_root(std::vector<int>& parent, int x)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n parent values. Line 3: x.

Output Format:
One line with the root of x.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= x < n

questions.title: Union and Find the Root
questions.description:
A tracker merges accounts by union-find: implement BOTH find_root (follow parent pointers to a self-parent) and union_sets — union_sets(a, b) roots a under the root of b... more precisely, it hangs the root of b beneath the root of a (parent[root_b] = root_a) and does nothing when they already share a root. Input format: line 1 has n and k; the next k lines each have a and b (one union); the last line has x. The harness initializes parent[i] = i, performs the k unions with YOUR union_sets and prints YOUR find_root(parent, x). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only these two functions:

    int find_root(std::vector<int>& parent, int x)
    void union_sets(std::vector<int>& parent, int a, int b)

Input Format:
Line 1: n and k. Next k lines: a b. Last line: x.

Output Format:
One line with the root of x after all unions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= k <= 100, 0 <= a, b, x < n
